title.source: Garmin戴上GPS，為何還不能立刻跑？｜品牌故事
title.text: Garmin put GPS on your wrist. Why couldn't you just run?｜Brand Story

description.source:
把GPS戴上手腕，還不等於一趟跑步記得好。從2003年11月出貨的Forerunner201，沿著充電與初次鎖星、配速平滑和目標夥伴、歷史保存與序列埠上傳，接到2006年205/305的腕旁天線、胸帶識別碼和記錄容量，再看2009長期使用者如何處理資料。

201手冊是2006年2月RevF，205/305手冊是RevD©2006–2008，不能把後期手冊全當首發韌體。15–30分鐘只指201初次定位，3.5小時指305每秒記錄的詳細資料容量。DC Rainmaker原帖2007，但本片採明示2009-06-25大幅更新的自述，非受控精度實驗；未採動態比較表、讀者留言或游泳建議。手機競爭沒有被寫成2003跑錶發明動機。畫面為匿名概念插畫。

description.text:
Putting GPS on your wrist doesn't automatically mean recording a run well. Starting with the Forerunner 201, shipped in November 2003, we follow charging and initial satellite acquisition, pace smoothing and a target partner, history storage and serial-port transfers. Then come the wrist-side antennas, chest-strap IDs and recording capacity of the 2006 205/305, followed by how a long-term user handled the data in 2009.

The 201 manual is February 2006 Rev F; the 205/305 manual is Rev D, ©2006–2008. Later manuals cannot all be treated as launch firmware. The 15–30 minutes applies only to the 201's initial position fix; 3.5 hours is the 305's detailed-data capacity when recording every second. DC Rainmaker's original post dates to 2007, but this video uses his account explicitly marked as substantially updated on 2009-06-25, not a controlled accuracy experiment. It excludes the dynamic comparison table, reader comments and swimming advice. Phone competition is not presented as the reason the 2003 running watch was invented. Visuals are anonymous conceptual illustrations.

chapters.source: 手腕上的錶，還在等天空
chapters.text: The watch on your wrist waits for the sky

chapters.source: 先充好電，再等訊號條消失
chapters.text: Charge first, then wait for the signal bar to vanish

chapters.source: 坐標變成配速，還得讓人看懂
重設之前，先把這一跑留下來
chapters.text: Save this run before the next reset

chapters.source: 天線沿著手腕，朝天空轉過去
chapters.text: An antenna curves around the wrist toward the sky

chapters.source: 記得更細，能留下的時間反而變短
二零零九年，記錄到了軟體裡

sources: Twenty years of running with Garmin
Garmin FY2003 Form 10-K, original SEC filing
DC Rainmaker: Review of GarminForerunner305; major2009update

lines.source: 在屋外，你按住Forerunner二零一的電源，衛星圖示還在閃。
lines.text: Outside, you hold down the Forerunner 201's power button. The satellite icon is still flashing.

lines.source: 如果你第一次定位，等待可能拖到十五至三十分鐘。
lines.text: If this is your first position fix, the wait could stretch to 15–30 minutes.

lines.source: 這是二零零六年二月修訂手冊裡，第一次起跑前的動作。
lines.text: These are the steps before your first run in the manual revised in February 2006.

lines.source: 電已充好，人也準備好了，手腕上的錶到底還在等什麼？
lines.text: The battery is charged and you're ready. What is the watch on your wrist still waiting for?

lines.source: 等你跑起來，螢幕裡的兩個小人，還會帶來另一個問題。
lines.text: Once you start running, the two little figures on the screen will raise another question.

lines.source: 到了二零零六年，另一支裝置，得先面對你不停擺動的手臂。
lines.text: By 2006, another device first had to deal with your constantly swinging arm.

lines.source: 我們沿著Garmin從定位到留下記錄的改動，追這段腕上GPS的路。
lines.text: We'll follow Garmin's changes, from finding your position to keeping a record, along this journey of wrist-worn GPS.

lines.source: 把GPS戴到手腕上，還差什麼，才能成為你用得上的跑步工具？
lines.text: Once GPS is on your wrist, what else does it need to become a running tool you can actually use?

lines.source: 要讓你的一跑留下記錄，起點是二零零三年十一月出貨的這款裝置。
lines.text: To leave a record of your run, our starting point is this device, first shipped in November 2003.

lines.source: 當年的公司年報，寫的是跑步時的速度、時間、距離和圈時。
lines.text: The company's annual report that year described speed, time, distance and lap times while running.

lines.source: 這款裝置的初步規格，列的重量是七十八公克。
lines.text: The preliminary specifications listed its weight as 78 grams.

lines.source: 它的長方形機身寬度超過八公分，厚度則不到兩公分。
lines.text: Its rectangular body was over 8 centimeters wide and less than 2 centimeters thick.

lines.source: 如果你要邊跑邊看，這塊裝置就得連同顯示畫面，一起留在手腕上。
lines.text: If you wanted to read it while running, the whole device, display included, had to stay on your wrist.

lines.source: 它早在車用導航後來碰上手機競爭以前，就進到跑者的手腕。
lines.text: It reached runners' wrists well before car navigation later faced competition from phones.

lines.source: 把這塊裝置帶出門，它的電要從哪裡來？
lines.text: When you took this device outside, where would its power come from?

lines.source: 它使用可充電鋰電池，手冊列充滿可用長達十五小時。
lines.text: It used a rechargeable lithium battery. The manual listed up to 15 hours of use on a full charge.

lines.source: 後來修訂的手冊又提醒，低溫、高溫和電池老化，都會減少電量。
lines.text: The later revised manual also warned that cold, heat and battery aging would all reduce available power.

lines.source: 所以你把接點擦乾，先把四接點那一端扣進充電座。
lines.text: So you dry the contacts, then clip the end with four contacts into the charging cradle first.

lines.source: 修訂手冊說，第一次使用前，要先充電至少兩小時。
lines.text: The revised manual says to charge it for at least two hours before first use.

lines.source: 一般充滿所需的時間，列在一到三小時之間。
lines.text: A normal full charge is listed as taking between one and three hours.

lines.source: 可是機器久置到電池完全沒電時，插上電源，螢幕就一定立刻有反應嗎？
lines.text: But if it has sat unused until the battery is completely drained, will the screen always respond as soon as you plug it in?

lines.source: 手冊說，這種情況可能得充電最多三十分鐘，才開機或顯示充電。
lines.text: The manual says that in this case, charging may take up to 30 minutes before it turns on or shows that it is charging.

lines.source: 因此，看到螢幕沒亮，還得先分清它是否正在補回電量。
lines.text: So if the screen stays dark, you first need to work out whether it is still recovering its charge.

lines.source: 電充進去了，錶又要怎麼知道，你現在站在哪裡？
lines.text: Once the power is in, how does the watch know where you're standing?

lines.source: 我覺得這個起點很有意思：人已經知道自己在哪，機器還不知道。
lines.text: I find this starting point interesting: you already know where you are, but the machine doesn't.

lines.source: 剛剛那本修訂手冊，把找訊號的條件寫得很具體。
lines.text: That revised manual spells out the conditions for finding a signal quite precisely.

lines.source: 第一次使用，要把它留在能清楚看見天空的地方。
lines.text: For first use, leave it somewhere with a clear view of the sky.

lines.source: 可是你每次出門，都得等那麼久嗎？
lines.text: But do you have to wait that long every time you head out?

lines.source: 前面的等待只指初次定位；同頁寫，之後找衛星通常不到幾分鐘。
lines.text: The earlier wait applies only to the initial position fix. The same page says later satellite acquisition usually takes less than a few minutes.

lines.source: 如果你急著跑出門，這兩種等待，差的可不是一點點。
lines.text: If you're in a hurry to get out for a run, those two waits are worlds apart.

lines.source: 但錶要找的是來自天空的訊號，屋頂和建物會把視野擋住。
lines.text: But the watch is looking for signals from the sky, and roofs and buildings block its view.

lines.source: 開場還在閃的衛星圖示，又要變成什麼樣，你才按開始？
lines.text: How must that flashing satellite icon from the opening change before you press Start?

lines.source: 衛星圖示停止閃爍，訊號條消失，才是它已經定位的提示。
lines.text: The satellite icon stops flashing and the signal bar disappears. Those are the signs that it has a position fix.

lines.source: 等到這時，按下開始鍵，這支錶才開始計時和追蹤距離。
lines.text: Only then do you press Start, and the watch begins timing and tracking distance.

lines.source: 可是，光知道你的位置，還不等於知道這一段跑得怎麼樣。
lines.text: But knowing your location alone doesn't tell you how that stretch of running went.

lines.source: 時間、配速和距離，出現在這支跑錶的運動主畫面上。
lines.text: Time, pace and distance appear on the running watch's main workout screen.

lines.source: 你按上下鍵，就能切到當圈的配速、圈時和圈距。
lines.text: Press the up and down buttons to switch to the current lap's pace, time and distance.

lines.source: 同一個位置資料，現在接上了時間，變成跑者要看的進度。
lines.text: The same position data is now paired with time, becoming the progress a runner wants to see.

lines.source: 但如果位置和速度有誤差，畫面上的配速，又該怎麼讀？
lines.text: But if position and speed contain errors, how should you read the pace on the screen?

lines.source: 它提供一個配速平滑設定，把一段時間裡的配速平均。
lines.text: It offers a pace-smoothing setting that averages pace over a period of time.

lines.source: 手冊說，這是為了避開GPS位置和速度計算的誤差。
lines.text: The manual says this is intended to avoid errors in GPS position and speed calculations.

lines.source: 設定裡可以選不同的平滑程度，最強到最弱都有。
lines.text: You can choose different smoothing levels, from strongest to weakest.

lines.source: 我會接著問，有了配速，你還得自己心算，才能追上目標嗎？
lines.text: My next question would be: once you have pace, do you still have to do mental arithmetic to keep up with your goal?

lines.source: 開場那兩個小人，這時才有了工作。
lines.text: Now those two little figures from the opening have a job.

lines.source: 你先輸入想跑的距離和時間，讓裝置建立一個目標。
lines.text: First, enter the distance and time you want to run, so the device can create a goal.

lines.source: 按下開始，畫面上方的虛擬夥伴，就照那個目標往前跑。
lines.text: Press Start, and the Virtual Partner at the top of the screen runs ahead according to that goal.

lines.source: 下方的小人代表你，底下會顯示兩邊相差多少。
lines.text: The figure below represents you, with the gap between you shown underneath.

lines.source: 畫面裡讓你追的人，是另一個真人嗎？
lines.text: Is the person you're chasing on the screen another real person?

lines.source: 這裡追的，是你事先設定的目標，並沒有另一個真人在線上跑。
lines.text: What you're chasing here is your preset goal. There isn't another real person running online.

lines.source: 但是，一趟跑步也會遇到紅燈，計時要一直算下去嗎？
lines.text: But runs can include red lights. Should the timer keep counting through them?

lines.source: 你可以設定，配速低於某個值時，自動暫停計時。
lines.text: You can set it to pause the timer automatically when your pace drops below a chosen value.

lines.source: 它到達暫停條件時，計時指示會閃爍。
lines.text: When the pause condition is met, the timer indicator flashes.

lines.source: 停下來的時間處理了，跑動中的分段，又能怎麼記？
lines.text: That deals with time spent stopped. How can you record segments while moving?

lines.source: 另一個自動記圈功能，則在到達設定距離時，替你記下一圈。
lines.text: A separate automatic lap function records a lap when you reach a set distance.

lines.source: 你也可以自己按圈鍵，告訴它這一段到這裡為止。
lines.text: You can also press the Lap button yourself to tell it this segment ends here.

lines.source: 手動停表再開始，裝置還會自動算成新的一圈。
lines.text: If you manually stop the timer and restart it, the device also automatically counts a new lap.

lines.source: 那麼跑完以後，這些分段和位置，能一起留下來嗎？
lines.text: So after your run, can those segments and positions all be kept together?

lines.source: 你停下計時，再按住重設鍵三秒，這一跑就成了上一次跑步。
lines.text: Stop the timer, then hold Reset for three seconds. This run becomes your last run.

lines.source: 手冊說，裝置會自動保存上一次跑步和歷史資料。
lines.text: The manual says the device automatically saves the last run and its history data.

lines.source: 我讀到這裡想問：存下歷史，就表示每一個點都保住了嗎？
lines.text: Reading this, I want to ask: does saving history mean every single point has survived?

lines.source: 手冊列的是，記憶體最多五千圈。
lines.text: The manual lists memory for up to 5,000 laps.

lines.source: 最近十次跑步有基本軌跡，而還沒重設的最近一跑，記得更細。
lines.text: The ten most recent runs have basic tracks, while the latest run, not yet reset, is recorded in more detail.

lines.source: 那一跑的詳細軌跡，最多能留三千個點。
lines.text: The detailed track for that run can hold up to 3,000 points.

lines.source: 如果你想保住最細的資料，要趕在哪個動作之前傳出去？
lines.text: If you want to preserve the finest detail, before which action must you transfer it?

lines.source: 手冊提醒，要在下次重設前傳到電腦，接收器就得接上另一端。
lines.text: The manual reminds you to transfer it to a computer before the next reset. The receiver needs a connection at the other end.

lines.source: 剛剛充電用的座子，現在要連起裝置與電腦。
lines.text: The cradle used for charging now has to connect the device and the computer.

lines.source: 這次，座上的序列線還要插到電腦的序列埠。
lines.text: This time, the cradle's serial cable also plugs into the computer's serial port.

lines.source: 打開訓練軟體，選接收歷史資料，才把活動傳進去。
lines.text: Open the training software and select Receive History to transfer the activity into it.

lines.source: 傳進電腦，只看過一次數字就結束了嗎？
lines.text: Once it's on the computer, does it end with a single look at the numbers?

lines.source: 在訓練軟體裡，你還可以加註記，把跑步歷史匯出成資料檔。
lines.text: In the training software, you can also add notes and export your running history as a data file.

lines.source: 若你要靠它導航回去，錶上的地圖又能畫得多細？
lines.text: If you want it to navigate you back, how detailed can the watch's map be?

lines.source: 它能開啟地圖模式，顯示自己走過的軌跡。
lines.text: You can turn on map mode to show the track you've followed.

lines.source: 它不能載入詳細地圖資料，畫面主要留下你和位置點。
lines.text: It cannot load detailed map data. The screen mainly shows you and location points.

lines.source: 選一個已存位置導航，裝置會從目前位置，拉出一條直線。
lines.text: Choose a saved location to navigate to, and the device draws a straight line from your current position.

lines.source: 如果直線中間有障礙，你還是得自己繞過去。
lines.text: If there's an obstacle along that line, you still have to find your own way around it.

lines.source: 可是只要手臂一直擺動，接收器還能好好看著天空嗎？
lines.text: But with your arm constantly swinging, can the receiver keep a good view of the sky?

lines.source: 二零五和三零五的規格，寫明片狀天線會在擺臂時朝向天空。
lines.text: The 205 and 305 specifications state that the patch antenna faces the sky as your arm swings.

lines.source: Garmin回顧開場那支裝置，說天線沿著手腕的一部分伸出去。
lines.text: Looking back at the device previewed in our opening, Garmin says its antenna extended around part of the wrist.

lines.source: 這段形狀，是為了讓天線取得更好的天空視野。
lines.text: That shape was intended to give the antenna a better view of the sky.

lines.source: 你抬手看螢幕的動作，和接收器要看的方向，得放在一起處理。
lines.text: The way you raise your hand to read the screen and the direction the receiver needs to face have to be handled together.

lines.source: 我看到這裡會問，接收器變了，你還需要先到開闊地找衛星嗎？
lines.text: At this point I'd ask: with a different receiver, do you still need to find satellites in an open area first?

lines.source: 規格也列出高感度接收器，但手冊並沒有因此叫你直接起跑。
lines.text: The specifications also list a high-sensitivity receiver, but the manual doesn't tell you to start running straight away.

lines.source: 它還是要求，到遠離高樓和樹木的開闊地方找衛星。
lines.text: It still calls for an open area, away from tall buildings and trees, to acquire satellites.

lines.source: 把天線朝上，先站定，等定位頁消失。
lines.text: Point the antenna upward, stand still and wait for the acquisition page to disappear.

lines.source: 如果你想知道身體出了多少力，速度以外，還能接到什麼資料？
lines.text: If you want to know how hard your body is working, what data can you receive besides speed?

lines.source: 三零五加入的心率資料，來自另一件貼在身上的東西。
lines.text: The heart-rate data added by the 305 comes from another item worn against your body.

lines.source: 胸帶要直接接觸皮膚，綁在胸骨下方。
lines.text: The chest strap must touch your skin directly and sit just below the breastbone.

lines.source: 你還得把背面的兩個感測點沾濕，讓脈搏和傳送器連上。
lines.text: You also wet the two sensing patches on the back to connect your pulse to the transmitter.

lines.source: 這份手冊的胸帶，三零五能用，同代二零五不支援。
lines.text: The chest strap in this manual works with the 305. The same-generation 205 does not support it.

lines.source: 不過你把胸帶戴好，錶又怎麼確定，收到的是你的資料？
lines.text: But once you've put the chest strap on, how does the watch know it's receiving your data?

lines.source: 每個感測器都有自己的識別碼，第一次配對時，這支錶會學起來。
lines.text: Each sensor has its own identification code, which the watch learns during the first pairing.

lines.source: 下次開機，它就用存下的識別碼，尋找那個感測器。
lines.text: The next time you turn it on, it uses that saved code to look for that sensor.

lines.source: 配對之後，手冊說它只接收這個感測器的資料。
lines.text: After pairing, the manual says it receives data only from that sensor.

lines.source: 配對時，你的錶和胸帶離多遠，才符合手冊的建議？
lines.text: How close must your watch and chest strap be during pairing to meet the manual's recommendation?

lines.source: 手冊要它們在三公尺內，還要遠離別人的感測器。
lines.text: The manual says within three meters of each other, and away from other people's sensors.

lines.source: 若看起來配到別人的感測器，排錯建議是重新掃描。
lines.text: If it seems to have paired with someone else's sensor, the troubleshooting advice is to scan again.

lines.source: 訊號接進來以後，儲存空間還得容得下這一跑。
lines.text: Once the signal is coming in, the storage still has to hold this run.

lines.source: 每一秒都留下，還是只留重要的變化？
lines.text: Keep every second, or just the important changes?

lines.source: 三零五預設的智慧記錄，按方向、速度或心率的變化選取關鍵點。
lines.text: The 305's default Smart Recording selects key points based on changes in direction, speed or heart rate.

lines.source: 如果改成每秒都記，能一直保留整趟活動嗎？
lines.text: If you switch to recording every second, can it keep the entire activity indefinitely?

lines.source: 但手冊接著寫，這樣最多只能記下三點五小時的詳細資料。
lines.text: But the manual goes on to say that this allows at most 3.5 hours of detailed data.

lines.source: 這是詳細資料的儲存上限，電池續航是另一項規格。
lines.text: That is a storage limit for detailed data. Battery endurance is a separate specification.

lines.source: 我會把它看成同一趟跑步的新取捨：不是每個點都能永遠留著。
lines.text: I see it as a new trade-off within the same run: not every point can be kept forever.

lines.source: 手冊又提醒，歷史滿了，較舊的資料會自動被覆寫。
lines.text: The manual also warns that when history is full, older data is automatically overwritten.

lines.source: 針對覆寫，手冊建議定期把歷史傳到電腦保存。
lines.text: To guard against overwriting, it recommends regularly transferring history to a computer for safekeeping.

lines.source: 留在歷史裡的活動，下一次出門還能做什麼？
lines.text: What can an activity saved in history do for your next outing?

lines.source: 你能在歷史裡挑一筆活動，用它建立一條路線。
lines.text: You can choose an activity from history and use it to create a course.

lines.source: 你再沿著它跑，目標就能換成追上過去那次表現。
lines.text: Run along it again, and your goal can become matching that earlier performance.

lines.source: 如果你想把補水處或轉彎留成提示，還可以加上路線點。
lines.text: If you want prompts for a water stop or turn, you can also add course points.

lines.source: 不過，這些路線點要用電腦上的訓練軟體加入。
lines.text: But those course points must be added in the training software on a computer.

lines.source: 傳回裝置後，畫面才會顯示，到下一個路線點還有多遠。
lines.text: Only after you transfer them back to the device does the screen show the distance to the next course point.

lines.source: 可是一條路線上，要怎麼同時看你和過去那次活動？
lines.text: But on one course, how can you see both yourself and that earlier activity?

lines.source: 地圖裡的灰色三角形，代表原本那次活動的進度。
lines.text: The gray triangle on the map represents the progress of the original activity.

lines.source: 黑色三角形，則是你現在的位置。
lines.text: The black triangle is your current position.

lines.source: 如果跑離路線，箭頭先引你回去；回去以後，它又要指哪裡？
lines.text: If you stray off course, the arrow first guides you back. Where does it point once you're back?

lines.source: 一旦回到路線，箭頭才繼續指示，沿著它該往哪裡走。
lines.text: Only once you're back on the course does the arrow resume showing which way to follow it.

lines.source: 規格裡能比較過去，真的長期跑下來，留下的會是什麼？
lines.text: The specifications let you compare with the past. After long-term running in practice, what actually remains?

lines.source: 評測者DC Rainmaker的三零五，留下了三百六十三次跑步。
lines.text: Reviewer DC Rainmaker's 305 recorded 363 runs.

lines.source: 這是他在二零零九年六月二十五日，大幅更新的長期評測自述。
lines.text: That is his account in the long-term review he substantially updated on June 25, 2009.

lines.source: 他報告的記錄，也會在遮蔽物旁遇到中斷嗎？
lines.text: Did the recordings he reported also suffer interruptions near obstructions?

lines.source: 他寫，一般樹木和較矮建物旁，通常沒有什麼問題。
lines.text: He wrote that ordinary trees and lower buildings generally caused little trouble.

lines.source: 但沿著較高的建物跑，有時會短暫失去連線。
lines.text: But running alongside taller buildings sometimes caused brief connection losses.

lines.source: 至於剛剛那種追目標的小人，他會拿來當自己的訓練依據嗎？
lines.text: As for those little figures chasing a goal, did he use them to guide his own training?

lines.source: 而且畫面上的小人，他自己其實用得不多。
lines.text: In fact, he didn't use the little figures on the screen very much.

lines.source: 因為他主要依心率訓練，所以更常看身體的反應。
lines.text: Because he trained mainly by heart rate, he looked more often at his body's response.

lines.source: 我覺得這個選擇很實在：能顯示的資料，不一定每一種都要追。
lines.text: I think that's a practical choice: you don't have to chase every kind of data a device can display.

lines.source: 同一趟活動，到了電腦曲線裡，就一定變得比較好讀嗎？
lines.text: Does the same activity necessarily become easier to read once it's plotted on a computer?

lines.source: 他展示過一個例子：某一秒的配速，突然跳出很高的尖峰。
lines.text: He showed an example in which the pace for a single second suddenly produced a very high spike.

lines.source: 在當時的內建軟體裡，他不能改資料點，也不能調整圖表刻度。
lines.text: In the bundled software at the time, he couldn't edit data points or adjust the chart scale.

lines.source: 你如果想替每次跑步命名、分組，這又要怎麼做？
lines.text: If you want to name and group each of your runs, how do you do that?

lines.source: 他寫自己已改用第三方軟體，能命名、分組，也能匯出資料。
lines.text: He wrote that he had switched to third-party software that could name, group and export the data.

lines.source: 如果你想比較兩次活動，記錄留下以後，怎麼整理也很重要。
lines.text: If you want to compare two activities, how you organize the records matters too.

lines.source: 開場那個等待，最後要交給你的，是看得懂也留得下的一趟活動。
lines.text: What that wait in the opening must ultimately give you is an activity you can understand and preserve.

lines.source: 如果你有跑步記錄，留言告訴我，你最常回頭看哪一項？
lines.text: If you keep running records, tell me in the comments: which measure do you look back at most often?

lines.source: 也訂閱我，讓這些平常只看見結果的設計，繼續被講清楚。
lines.text: And subscribe, so we can keep explaining the designs whose results are usually all we see.
